items.title: Corteva CEO Sees Expansion From Corn Into Strawberries
items.summary: Corteva Chief Executive Chuck Magro says the company’s soon-to-be spun-off seed business, Vylor, could expand beyond corn and soybeans and into fruits and vegetables, aided by gene-editing advancements.

items.title: Corteva Says Farmers Are Willing to Pay Up for High-Tech Seeds
items.summary: Since the advent of Roundup Ready crops designed to withstand potent weedkillers, seeds and sprays have been entwined in the agriculture industry. Chuck Magro, CEO of Corteva, wants to undo that: Next month, his $55 billion company will split, creating separate businesses focusing on seeds and pesticides.
